correctness.rationale: The 2D characteristic-two example has only identity automorphism via its distinguished idempotent and the unique square root of one in characteristic two. The 3D example has identity automorphism over any field by linear independence of u,v, orthogonality, and forcing images of all three basis vectors. Explicit invertible orthogonal natural-base parameter families have finite parameter fibers, hence give infinitely many classes over infinite fields. The char-not-two 2D lower bound splits perfect versus rank-one multiplication and constructs a nonidentity similarity fixing the multiplication generator using reflection or a hyperbolic basis. One-dimensional bases have one monomial equivalence class. Actual finite-field checker independently tests the explicit 2D and 3D algebras; no finite enumeration is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Question 14 explicitly asks whether infinitely many natural bases can coexist with a finite automorphism group in nondegenerate evolution algebras. The result gives explicit trivial-group examples and determines the least dimension over every infinite field, showing a genuine characteristic-two versus other-characteristic boundary. This answers the published question in its strong existence form rather than supplying an arbitrary example or a finite table. It also exhibits distinct rigidity of algebra automorphisms and flexibility of natural coordinates.
